Upload a `.tif`/`.tiff` elevation model (DEM), click the map (or type
coordinates) to place an observer, and see which cells are visible
from that point — accounting for terrain occlusion.

::: {.callout-tip}
**Private by design.** Your file is processed entirely in your
browser (R via WebAssembly) — it's never uploaded to any server,
including ours. Nothing to configure, nothing to trust: the code
never gets the chance to see your data.
:::

The code itself isn't shown here — it's a fixed, non-editable
computation using `terra::viewshed()` underneath. Want to see it
built up step by step (and read why this tool runs on R, not Python)?
Read
[Viewshed: What's Visible from Here](/posts/raster-viewshed.html).

```{.webgeods-r #viewshed-inspect-r .tool-cell}
#| package: terra, jsonlite, codetools
library(terra)

path <- NULL
for (candidate in c("/uploaded.tif")) {
  ok <- tryCatch({ rast(candidate); TRUE }, error = function(e) FALSE)
  if (ok) { path <- candidate; break }
}

summary_out <- NULL
footprint <- list(type = jsonlite::unbox("FeatureCollection"), features = list())

if (!is.null(path)) {
  r <- rast(path)
  # Only the first band is treated as elevation -- a DEM is normally
  # single-band; extra bands (if any) are simply ignored, same
  # reasoning as every raster tool on this site that only needs one
  # value per pixel.
  elevation <- r[[1]]

  # Same missing-CRS convention as the rest of the Raster family:
  # unknown stays unknown, never silently relabeled as WGS84. Here the
  # stakes are higher than a display nuance -- viewshed cannot pick a
  # working projection or place an observer without knowing where on
  # Earth the file actually is, so Compute refuses outright on a
  # CRS-less file (see viewshed-r below) rather than guessing.
  crs_label <- if (crs(elevation) == "") {
    NULL
  } else {
    crs_desc <- crs(elevation, describe = TRUE)
    if (!is.na(crs_desc$authority) && !is.na(crs_desc$code)) {
      paste0(crs_desc$authority, ":", crs_desc$code)
    } else {
      crs(elevation, proj = TRUE)
    }
  }

  e <- ext(elevation)
  bbox_wkt <- paste0(
    "POLYGON((",
    e$xmin, " ", e$ymin, ", ", e$xmax, " ", e$ymin, ", ",
    e$xmax, " ", e$ymax, ", ", e$xmin, " ", e$ymax, ", ",
    e$xmin, " ", e$ymin, "))"
  )
  bbox_vect <- vect(bbox_wkt, crs = if (crs(elevation) == "") "EPSG:4326" else crs(elevation))
  bbox_wgs84 <- tryCatch(project(bbox_vect, "EPSG:4326"), error = function(err) bbox_vect)
  bbox_geom <- geom(bbox_wgs84)
  footprint_coords <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(bbox_geom)), function(i) c(bbox_geom[i, "x"], bbox_geom[i, "y"]))

  footprint <- list(
    type = jsonlite::unbox("FeatureCollection"),
    features = list(list(
      type = jsonlite::unbox("Feature"),
      properties = list(name = jsonlite::unbox("DEM footprint")),
      geometry = list(type = jsonlite::unbox("Polygon"), coordinates = list(footprint_coords))
    ))
  )

  summary_out <- list(
    width = jsonlite::unbox(ncol(elevation)),
    height = jsonlite::unbox(nrow(elevation)),
    crs = if (is.null(crs_label)) NULL else jsonlite::unbox(crs_label),
    bounds = round(c(e$xmin, e$ymin, e$xmax, e$ymax), 6)
  )
}

result <- list(summary = summary_out, footprint = footprint)
jsonlite::fromJSON(jsonlite::toJSON(result, null = "null"), simplifyVector = FALSE)
```

```{.webgeods-r #viewshed-r .tool-cell}
#| inject: [obsLon, obsLat, obsHeight]
#| package: terra, jsonlite, codetools
library(terra)

r <- rast(path)
elevation <- r[[1]]

if (crs(elevation) == "") {
  stop("This file has no declared CRS — a real-world location is required to compute a viewshed (to choose a working projection and place the observer correctly). Upload a georeferenced DEM.")
}

original_crs_label <- {
  crs_desc <- crs(elevation, describe = TRUE)
  if (!is.na(crs_desc$authority) && !is.na(crs_desc$code)) {
    paste0(crs_desc$authority, ":", crs_desc$code)
  } else {
    crs(elevation, proj = TRUE)
  }
}

# Working/calculation CRS: terra::viewshed() requires projected
# coordinates (confirmed empirically -- it throws "the method does
# not support lon/lat data" otherwise). A geographic DEM is
# reprojected HERE, for this calculation only -- the original raster
# is never modified, and the CRS reported above is the file's real
# one, not this working projection. The UTM zone is picked from the
# raster's own centre -- a reasonable default for a single local DEM,
# not a universally correct choice (a DEM spanning multiple UTM
# zones, near the poles, or very large would need a deliberate choice
# instead).
if (is.lonlat(elevation)) {
  e <- ext(elevation)
  center_lon <- (e$xmin + e$xmax) / 2
  center_lat <- (e$ymin + e$ymax) / 2
  utm_zone <- floor((center_lon + 180) / 6) + 1
  calc_epsg <- if (center_lat >= 0) 32600 + utm_zone else 32700 + utm_zone
  elevation_calc <- project(elevation, paste0("EPSG:", calc_epsg), method = "bilinear")
} else {
  elevation_calc <- elevation
}

calc_crs_label <- {
  crs_desc <- crs(elevation_calc, describe = TRUE)
  if (!is.na(crs_desc$authority) && !is.na(crs_desc$code)) {
    paste0(crs_desc$authority, ":", crs_desc$code)
  } else {
    crs(elevation_calc, proj = TRUE)
  }
}

# The observer point always arrives as lon/lat (map click or manual
# input) and is reprojected into whatever the calculation CRS turned
# out to be -- whether or not the raster itself needed reprojecting.
obs_pt <- vect(matrix(c(as.numeric(obsLon), as.numeric(obsLat)), ncol = 2), crs = "EPSG:4326")
obs_pt_calc <- project(obs_pt, crs(elevation_calc))
obs_xy <- as.numeric(crds(obs_pt_calc)[1, ])

vs <- viewshed(elevation_calc, loc = obs_xy, observer = as.numeric(obsHeight), target = 0)

# NaN renders transparent on the map, so "not visible" becomes NaN
# instead of FALSE/0 -- only the visible area actually paints.
vs_num <- as.numeric(values(vs, mat = FALSE))
visible_mask <- vs_num == 1
vs_num[!visible_mask] <- NaN
vs_num[visible_mask] <- 1

n_visible <- sum(visible_mask, na.rm = TRUE)
n_total <- length(vs_num)

e_calc <- ext(elevation_calc)
bbox_wkt <- paste0(
  "POLYGON((",
  e_calc$xmin, " ", e_calc$ymin, ", ", e_calc$xmax, " ", e_calc$ymin, ", ",
  e_calc$xmax, " ", e_calc$ymax, ", ", e_calc$xmin, " ", e_calc$ymax, ", ",
  e_calc$xmin, " ", e_calc$ymin, "))"
)
bbox_vect <- vect(bbox_wkt, crs = crs(elevation_calc))
bbox_wgs84 <- tryCatch(project(bbox_vect, "EPSG:4326"), error = function(err) bbox_vect)
bbox_geom <- geom(bbox_wgs84)
footprint_coords <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(bbox_geom)), function(i) c(bbox_geom[i, "x"], bbox_geom[i, "y"]))
e_wgs84 <- ext(bbox_wgs84)

footprint <- list(
  type = jsonlite::unbox("FeatureCollection"),
  features = list(list(
    type = jsonlite::unbox("Feature"),
    properties = list(name = jsonlite::unbox("viewshed footprint")),
    geometry = list(type = jsonlite::unbox("Polygon"), coordinates = list(footprint_coords))
  ))
)

# Encodes the pixel array as base64 float32 bytes via
# rawConnection()+writeBin()+jsonlite::base64_enc().
con <- rawConnection(raw(0), "wb")
writeBin(vs_num, con, size = 4, endian = "little")
raw_bytes <- rawConnectionValue(con)
close(con)
data_b64 <- jsonlite::base64_enc(raw_bytes)

summary_out <- list(
  width = jsonlite::unbox(ncol(vs)),
  height = jsonlite::unbox(nrow(vs)),
  data = jsonlite::unbox(data_b64),
  wgs84Bounds = round(c(e_wgs84$xmin, e_wgs84$ymin, e_wgs84$xmax, e_wgs84$ymax), 6),
  originalCrs = jsonlite::unbox(original_crs_label),
  calculationCrs = jsonlite::unbox(calc_crs_label),
  observerHeight = jsonlite::unbox(as.numeric(obsHeight)),
  visiblePixels = jsonlite::unbox(n_visible),
  totalPixels = jsonlite::unbox(n_total),
  visiblePercent = jsonlite::unbox(round(100 * n_visible / n_total, 1))
)

result_out <- list(summary = summary_out, footprint = footprint)
jsonlite::fromJSON(jsonlite::toJSON(result_out, null = "null"), simplifyVector = FALSE)
```

```{.webgeods-r #viewshed-export-r .tool-cell}
#| inject: [obsLon, obsLat, obsHeight]
#| package: terra, jsonlite, codetools
# Recomputes the same viewshed (cheap relative to re-reading the
# source file) and writes it as an actual GeoTIFF via writeRaster() —
# in the CALCULATION crs (the projection the computation actually ran
# in), not the original file's CRS, since re-reprojecting the result
# back just for convenience would add a step with no real benefit —
# the download button below labels this explicitly.
library(terra)

r <- rast(path)
elevation <- r[[1]]

if (is.lonlat(elevation)) {
  e <- ext(elevation)
  center_lon <- (e$xmin + e$xmax) / 2
  center_lat <- (e$ymin + e$ymax) / 2
  utm_zone <- floor((center_lon + 180) / 6) + 1
  calc_epsg <- if (center_lat >= 0) 32600 + utm_zone else 32700 + utm_zone
  elevation_calc <- project(elevation, paste0("EPSG:", calc_epsg), method = "bilinear")
} else {
  elevation_calc <- elevation
}

obs_pt <- vect(matrix(c(as.numeric(obsLon), as.numeric(obsLat)), ncol = 2), crs = "EPSG:4326")
obs_pt_calc <- project(obs_pt, crs(elevation_calc))
obs_xy <- as.numeric(crds(obs_pt_calc)[1, ])

vs <- viewshed(elevation_calc, loc = obs_xy, observer = as.numeric(obsHeight), target = 0)

out_path <- "/tmp/viewshed.tif"
writeRaster(vs, out_path, overwrite = TRUE, filetype = "GTiff")
raw_bytes <- readBin(out_path, what = "raw", n = file.info(out_path)$size)
jsonlite::base64_enc(raw_bytes)
```

*First run loads the R engine — expect 1-3 minutes (R's WebAssembly
build is noticeably slower to start than this site's Python tools).
Instant after that, and again each time you come back to this page.*
